review_text: SKY TV used to be Britains most groundbreaking TV service, and specifically Sky Sports was arguably the greatest sports TV service the world had to offer. What we have had for the last 20 years is a slow decline, and is the result of the 'wokeification' of our nation. I won't get political, but its hard not too when all our favourite Soccer Saturday presenters are booted off the show in favour of soul less boring presenters and pundits. What happened to the glory days of Merson, Nicholls, Stelling and Kamara. I am only 30 years old, so you can hardly tell me that I'm some old grumpy man who needs to get with the times - its just CRAP TV. The people who pay for Sky Sports - ie the target demographic - is clearly Men aged 30+. They are the ones with higher salarys, usually stay in at weekend and will want a full TV package. Why do they not understand who the target demographic is? We do not want spiky haired females or Eni Aluko lecturing us.What's with the constant pushing of race baiters like Eni Aluko by Sky Sports? Trying to cause division in our country. She even had the galls to try and send for Ian Wright.It's time US the consumer started having a backbone, and just cancelling your sky sports package. I would say go even further and get rid of the whole lot, Sky as a whole does not even have the best exclusives now. If anything they are the bottom of the pile, have rubbish films on the movie section, and you are essentially paying Sky TV prices to just watch channels that would be on Freeview. Sky Sports is the exception however - I am a big Football and F1 fan, with a brief interest in Darts. I am only 30 but even I remember not that long ago, not needing Sky Sports and still being able to watch EVERY F1 race, and the majority of European games free mid week. Sky Sports has just bought everything, created a monopoly, and is cornering the market to force us all into having a TV subscription after everything included, will usually be £60-£100. Absolutely ludicrous, you can get basically the same with no sports for £8 a month if you only had netflix and free view. Sky needs to cut costs for the consumer, this is not some modern futuristic high tech service now. Its billy basic, and people only have Sky for the Sports now. However as soon as the Premier League gets their own streaming service, Sky will be defunct. Customers will not want to stay loyal to someone who has fleeced them for so long.

review_text: Sky Sports used to be the gold standard. Proper analysis, strong opinions, and pundits who weren’t afraid to upset someone’s nan. You’d finish a show having actually learned something about football.Now it feels like everyone’s had media training, a sensitivity briefing, and a reminder to “smile more” before going on air.Every discussion is so PC and careful it’s like watching a workplace induction video. Female presenters should stick to commentating on female football. No one disagrees, no one raises their voice, and any opinion stronger than “he did well there” gets quietly escorted out of the studio.The punditry has become especially painful. A lot of chat, very little insight, and analysis so obvious you can predict it before it’s said. “He wanted it more.” “Fine margins.” “It’s about character.” Cheers lads, really breaking new ground there.As for the pace of the shows — slow, polite, and utterly harmless. Football is tribal, emotional and chaotic, but Sky now presents it like a group therapy session where everyone’s feelings matter and no one’s allowed to be wrong.It still looks amazing in HD, mind you. Crystal clear visuals, pristine graphics… shame the excitement’s been left in standard definition somewhere around 2010.

review_text: I've been a long-standing BT Sport customer for many years and find the service infuriating. The content is good, but there are two major problems which are incredibly frustrating. First, the editorial of web and app content is an inconsistent mess. Some weeks you will find the event replay you want on the website only, another week it will be on the BT Player only, another week it will only be on the mobile app, etc etc. You get the picture. And, it will never be in the same place: Sometimes it will be in spoiler free, sometimes it will not so inevitably you often end up with spoilers. But, basically you have to go hunting round for the event you want through three different platforms sometimes I don't know why they make it so damn difficult to find content, because it's never where you think it will be.Secondly. All platforms are incredibly buggy and prone to faults and crashing. It doesn't matter if you use PC, Laptop, mobile, tablet, if you use this browser or that. The content is CONSTANTLY crashing or sometimes, like tonight (UFC Sterling Vs O'malley even replay) it simply won't play at all (it's not on the website at all , only on BT Player. Why? It doesn't really matter since the player crashes or just won't play it anyway). If you have to use BT Sport because it's your only way to view a particular sport then fair enough. But, if you have any other option then to save your sanity watch it else where with another broadcaster/provider.

review_text: Wow!  Where to even begin...ESPN has wormed its way into controlling so much of the sporting world that they need to be broken up by the FTC for anti-trust violations.  I finally gave in and upgraded my Hulu to one of the bundles that included ESPN in order to watch a few games that are only available through ESPN.  I selected what I thought was a premium bundle without commercials.  Apparently, "premium" includes ESPN Select.  Now my only experience with ESPN is what you get on cable, such as ESPN, ESPN 2, ESPNU. SEC Network, etc.  Apparently, my "premium" subscription only includes items that were previously only available on ESPN + (whatever that is).  When I realized my new upgrade would not let me watch the game I was trying to watch I called customer service who explained the ESPN Select subscription does not include ESPN, nor does it include items on ESPN 2, ESPNU, or the SEC Network.  Nope!  It only includes items previously on ESPN +, which are the games that could never even make ESPN8!  You know, community college men's hacky sack games!  So to get any teams that anyone has ever heard of, you have to get an additional upgrade for even more money!  Now don't dare make this mistake mid game like I did!  I had planned to watch most of the game out and watch the rest on my newly upgraded subscription when I returned home.  Ha!  Nope!  The game wouldn't load because it wasn't a women's basketball game from Orlando community College!  So when I called customer service to figure out why my football game wouldn't load, he explained to me that I bought the Temu ESPN subscription that didn't play any sports anyone actually wants to watch.  So I said let's upgrade this so I can catch the last of the game.  Poor guy had to read 20 minutes of disclaimers while I'm cussing under my breath as I'm missing the last of my game.  Then he finally finished and I was able to log in as the game ended.  Now all of this feels like some horrible deja vu because last year I went through a similar process where I upgraded, the game wouldn't play, so I canceled the very next day.  I was refunded, my services canceled, and then they charged me for the bundle I had cancelled for the next 13 months!  I finally realized this when I had the stupid idea to try this again, only to find I had been paying for it for the last 13 months!  In all fairness, I should have watched my bill and I could have corrected this a year ago, but everything is automatic these days.  The customer service reps were always super nice, but they work for a horrible company .  After this experience, I will pay my month to watch the rest of college football season and I will immediately cancel.  In fact, my experience was so annoying, I will probably cancel the entire bundle and Disney, Hulu, and especially ESPN can go bankrupt fore all I care.  They are a horrible company, I hope their stock tanks, and the idiots that run the company go unemployed.   Why even offer ESPN Select?  It is truly the TEMU of the sporting world.

review_text: ​Oh, Joy! The People’s Games (Behind a Paywall)​Isn’t it just heartwarming? The BBC—our stalwart champion of "free" public broadcasting—has heroically decided to protect us from the burden of watching the Commonwealth Games for free. In a stunning display of generosity, they’ve "passed the torch" to TNT Sports. Now, instead of the inconvenience of just turning on the TV, we get the privilege of paying a monthly subscription fee to see a hurdle cleared. Truly, it’s a victory for the common man’s wallet.​And let’s hear it for Glasgow! While those "frugal" Australians looked at the massive bill and said, "No thanks, we’d rather keep our economy intact," Glasgow stepped up like the friend who offers to buy the whole pub a round when they’ve forgotten their wallet.​The city and its taxpayers are practically tripping over themselves to welcome the expenses. Because if there is one thing a city needs more than functioning infrastructure, it’s the fleeting glory of hosting a sporting event that half the world forgot was happening.​I genuinely hope the games are a "splendid" time for everyone involved. After all, nothing says "community spirit" like a sporting festival you have to pay a premium to witness from your own living room.​Glasgow East.......
